nodes.label: Save Root Resolution
nodes.rationale: A base mod's save_root becomes the application name used for per-user data resolution; changing it silently relocates existing saves.

nodes.label: Featured Provider Visibility
nodes.rationale: The featured flag gates whether a provider appears in the UI picker.

nodes.label: Additive Mod Schema Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Adding mod.toml fields is safe, while renaming or removing stored fields breaks deserialization of saves that retain the schema.

nodes.label: CLAUDE Agent Scope Alias
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is a filesystem symlink to AGENTS.md, exposing the same mod-registry guidance under the Claude convention.

nodes.label: Byte-Identical NPC Catalog Round Trip
nodes.rationale: Split and join tooling must reproduce the checked-in canonical four-space npcs.json byte for byte.

nodes.label: Prompt Placeholder Residue Guard
nodes.rationale: Rendering every testbed prompt and rejecting leftover placeholder tokens closes the coverage gap left by Rundale-only prompt tests.

nodes.label: Debt Scanner False-Positive Prevention
nodes.rationale: Rewording an intentional in-world TODO label as a regression reference prevents debt scanners from treating prompt content as unresolved engineering work.

nodes.label: Provider Mod Conventions Test
nodes.rationale: A checked-in fixture test catches provider directory, identity, visibility, URL, and preset coverage drift before it reaches onboarding or the UI.

nodes.label: Runtime Prompt Loading
nodes.source_location: opening scope description and Local gotchas
nodes.rationale: Prompt paths are declared in mod.toml and read at startup so a mod can replace dialogue behavior without compiling templates into the engine; missing files therefore fail startup with PromptsLoadError.

nodes.label: Case-Sensitive Placeholder Substitution
nodes.rationale: Template variable names must exactly match the runtime substitutions because unknown placeholders pass through verbatim without a warning.

nodes.label: Tier 1 Dual-Prompt Assembly
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 NPCs combine a character-defining system prompt with a separate scene-context prompt, while Tier 2 NPCs receive only their background-simulation system prompt.

nodes.label: Mod Prompt Override Pattern
nodes.rationale: The testbed mod uses visibly different pig-Latin templates to prove that prompt behavior is supplied by the active mod rather than hard-coded by the engine.

nodes.label: Anachronism Correction Loop
nodes.rationale: Detected terms from anachronisms.json produce corrective context in the next NPC prompt, reinforcing the period-language guidance across turns.

nodes.label: CLAUDE Prompt Scope Alias
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is a filesystem symlink to AGENTS.md, exposing the same prompt-scope guidance to tools that discover CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Runtime Scene State
nodes.rationale: The prompt grounds the NPC in the current location name and description, time, season, weather, and additional scene context.

nodes.label: Player Action Context
nodes.rationale: The player's current action is quoted as what the newcomer says, letting Tier 1 dialogue respond to the actual turn.

nodes.label: Tier 1 Character Role
nodes.rationale: The system prompt binds name, age, occupation, personality, guidance, and mood into a high-fidelity NPC role in 1820 County Roscommon.

nodes.label: Occupational Knowledge Boundaries
nodes.rationale: NPCs redirect or admit ignorance outside the expertise of their authored occupation, preventing generic all-knowing characters.

nodes.label: 1820 Rural Roscommon World Facts
nodes.rationale: The prompt fixes the political, educational, linguistic, agricultural, and technological conditions of Ireland in 1820, including emancipation and famine events that have not yet occurred.

nodes.label: Historical Anachronism Guard
nodes.source_location: WORLD FACTS, HISTORICAL CONTEXT, and REGISTER
nodes.rationale: Explicit dates, unavailable technologies, travel and news constraints, and banned modern register keep NPC responses inside the 1820 setting.

nodes.label: Dignified Irish Character Portrayal
nodes.rationale: The prompt requires warm, intelligent, resilient, complex characters and forbids stage-Irish stereotypes involving drunkenness, violence, foolish superstition, or exaggerated dialect.

nodes.label: Restricted Irish Phrase Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Only eight enumerated Irish expressions may be used verbatim; forbidding invented phrases and improvised grammar prevents fabricated Irish-language output.

nodes.label: Hiberno-English Period Register
nodes.rationale: A restrained set of dialect markers and period equivalents produces regional voice while avoiding modern vocabulary and caricature.

nodes.label: Conversation Farewell Discipline
nodes.rationale: Parting phrases are reserved for an explicit player departure so an NPC does not accidentally close an ongoing conversation.

nodes.label: In-Character Dialogue Only
nodes.rationale: The visible response contains only words spoken aloud, with no narration or action tags; physical behavior belongs in structured metadata.

nodes.label: Concise Dialogue Contract
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 replies are constrained to two to four conversational sentences rather than monologues.

nodes.label: Tier 1 Metadata Contract
nodes.rationale: Every spoken reply is followed by an exact separator and JSON object containing action, mood, internal thought, and language hints.

nodes.label: Tier 2 Background Interaction Simulation
nodes.rationale: Tier 2 models ambient interactions among characters present in an 1820 Irish parish without direct player-action context.

nodes.label: Background Scene State
nodes.rationale: Location, time, weather, and the characters present ground each Tier 2 simulation.

nodes.label: Ambient Interaction Summary
nodes.rationale: The simulation returns a brief one-to-two-sentence account of what background characters do and say.

nodes.label: Tier 2 Relationship Changes
nodes.rationale: Directed from/to NPC identifiers encode relationship changes caused by the simulated interaction.

nodes.label: Bounded Relationship Delta
nodes.rationale: Each relationship adjustment is numerically constrained to the interval from -0.1 to 0.1.

nodes.label: Tier 2 JSON Output Contract
nodes.rationale: The entire Tier 2 response is one JSON object with summary, mood_changes, and relationship_changes fields.

nodes.label: Testbed Conceptual Scope Guard
nodes.rationale: Flags terminology outside the testbed's conceptual scope so dialogue can redirect naturally instead of accepting an unsupported concept.

nodes.label: Natural Redirection
nodes.rationale: The guard instructs dialogue to redirect an out-of-scope term naturally.

nodes.label: Engine Testbed
nodes.rationale: A minimal blueprint-aesthetic world exists to verify and exercise the Parish game engine.

nodes.label: Reduced-Fidelity NPC Simulation
nodes.rationale: Tier 2 uses a short in-character response to simulate an NPC at reduced fidelity.

nodes.label: Rundale App Icon
nodes.rationale: A square, rounded-corner game icon combines an ornate capital R with a dim rural landscape to express Rundale's historical Irish setting.

nodes.label: Illuminated-Manuscript Knotwork
nodes.source_location: ornamental strokes inside and around the capital R
nodes.rationale: Interlaced loops and spiral terminals make the monogram resemble Insular illuminated lettering.

nodes.label: Sepia Parchment Palette
nodes.rationale: Warm ochre highlights, brown ink-like outlines, and dark vignetted corners give the icon an aged parchment or illuminated-page appearance.
